notes: SFCC site, direct HTTP fetch. Checked header mega-menu (top-level nav item labelled 'Last Remaining Pieces', linking to /en/last-chance-exclusives), footer, and sitemap_4-category.xml for clearance/outlet/sale/discontinued-style slugs. Candidates found and adjudicated: (1) https://www.tanagra.me/en/last-chance-exclusives -- H1='Last Remaining Pieces', title tag 'Discover Luxury Last Remaining Pieces | Tanagra UAE', real product grid, data-total-product-count=616 (500 unique data-pid tiles loaded at sz=500, page itself reports [500]/616 items -- qty taken from the site's own total-count attribute, not from counting loaded tiles). URL slug 'last-chance-exclusives' matches the brief's 'Last Chance' target term and the H1 reads as end-of-line/last-piece merchandising, which is why it is recorded here. However the on-page banner copy is 'Don't miss out on limited-time pieces. Shop exclusive designs before they're gone for good' (framed as scarcity of exclusive/limited-edition items, not a markdown sale), and price-check across the sampled tiles found NO discounting anywhere: every item_category-tagged GTM impression on the page reports discount:0 and every tile has data-on-sales="false" (checked ~4000 repeated JSON blocks across the loaded tiles, all discount:0). So this reads as a 'last few pieces of exclusive/limited-edition stock' curated page rather than a classic price-marked-down clearance/outlet listing -- genuinely ambiguous per the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test, hence flagged for manual review rather than silently included or excluded. (2) https://www.tanagra.me/en/staff-sale -- rejected: page requires sign-in with a Tanagra work email ('Sign-in to your Tanagra account with your work email address'), i.e. an internal employee-only benefit page, not a public clearance PLP (data-total-product-count=2, consistent with a gated stub). (3) https://www.tanagra.me/en/limited-time-offer -- rejected: H1='Limited Time Offer', banner copy is about a gift-with-purchase promo ('Indulge in a curated gift with your purchase, exclusively for you'), a temporary promotional campaign with no permanence/clearance signal (its <title> tag is a stale/misconfigured copy of the Bestsellers page's title, which is why it surfaced in an initial keyword sweep, but the actual page content is unrelated to Bestsellers or Clearance). Excluded per brief Section 3 (temporary promo / GWP campaign, no discount/clearance signal).

rows.evidence: data-total-product-count="616" / data-template="[500] / 616 items" (site's own PLP total-count attribute; 500 of 616 tiles loaded at sz=500 sample)
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS SALE/CLEARANCE - URL slug 'last-chance-exclusives' and H1 'Last Remaining Pieces' match Clearance target terms (Last Chance/end-of-line), but banner copy frames it as scarce exclusive/limited-edition designs ('before they're gone for good'), not a price markdown, and every sampled product tile shows discount:0 / data-on-sales=false (no price cuts found anywhere on the page). Could be genuine end-of-line clearance merchandising (luxury retailers often clear stock without discounting) or could be a non-clearance 'exclusive scarcity' marketing category -- needs human judgment on whether this project intends non-discounted last-piece/end-of-line listings to count as Clearance.
